messages.content:
Work out the ICD-10-AM principal diagnosis category for the episode below. The principal diagnosis is the single condition established after investigation to be chiefly responsible for the patient's episode of admitted care. It is not the patient's most serious comorbidity, not the presenting symptom, and not the procedure performed.

Think in three steps: first name the condition chiefly responsible for the admission, second name the ICD-10-AM chapter letter it belongs to, third give the three-character category.

Example 1
Hospital course: A 72-year-old man with a 50 pack-year smoking history was admitted with three days of worsening breathlessness and purulent sputum. Spirometry showed an FEV1/FVC ratio of 0.52. He was treated with nebulised bronchodilators, oral prednisolone and antibiotics for an infective exacerbation of his long-standing airflow limitation.
Answer: Irreversible airflow limitation in a heavy smoker with an infective exacerbation is chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, chapter J, category J44.
CODE: J44

Example 2
Hospital course: A 58-year-old man presented with crushing central chest pain radiating to the jaw. The electrocardiogram showed ST elevation in the anterior leads and high-sensitivity troponin rose from 40 to 2100 ng/L. He underwent primary percutaneous coronary intervention with a stent to the proximal left anterior descending artery.
Answer: ST elevation with a rising troponin and culprit-vessel stenting is an acute myocardial infarction, chapter I, category I21.
CODE: I21

Hospital course:
Hospital Course Summary:

This 47-year-old male patient was admitted to our institution with a diagnosis of acute myeloid leukemia (AML) with multiple mutations, including DNMT3A, RUNX1, and U2AF1, along with FLT3–ITD mutation. The patient had received various treatments for his condition but did not respond well to them. After a bone marrow analysis, emergent BCR–ABL1 rearrangement was detected along with increased allelic ratio of FLT3-ITD mutation. The patient was then treated with different therapies, including CPX-351 plus venetoclax, ponatinib, and gilteritinib combination, which resulted in a marrow remission. The patient underwent allogeneic stem-cell transplantation (ASCT) and achieved full remission on day 30 post-ASCT. Unfortunately, the patient expired 8 months after ASCT due to infectious complications.

Summary of Hospital Stay:
Diagnosis: [diagnosis section withheld]
Treatment: CPX-351, decitabine, FLAG-IDA, single-agent gilteritinib, cladribine, idarubicin, cytarabine, sorafenib, decitabine, venetoclax, ponatinib, CPX-351 plus venetoclax, ponatinib, and gilteritinib combination, Allogeneic stem-cell transplantation
Complications: infectious complications
Outcome: Achieved Marrow remission; Achieved full remission post-ASCT

Assessment and Plan:

The patient presented with AML with FLT3–ITD, DNMT3A, RUNX1, and U2AF1 mutations that were resistant to several chemotherapy treatments. After various therapies, the patient achieved a marrow remission with the CPX-351 plus venetoclax, ponatinib, and gilteritinib combination. Allogeneic stem-cell transplantation was performed, which resulted in full remission post-ASCT. Despite successful remission, the patient died eight months post-ASCT due to infectious complications.

Write your reasoning in at most three short sentences, then a final line of exactly 'CODE: <letter><digit><digit>'.

text:
The condition chiefly responsible for this admission is refractory acute myeloid leukaemia with FLT3-ITD and emergent BCR–ABL1, treated with salvage therapy and allogeneic stem-cell transplantation. It belongs to chapter C, neoplasms. The category is C92, myeloid leukaemia.
CODE: C92
